name: Chiamaka Aguilar-Annan
role: Infrastructure disruption and industrial sabotage — saboteur
location: The Circuit — neon-lit entertainment and vice district
description:
Chiamaka Aguilar-Annan are lean and angular, all sharp edges and visible tension. At 43, they have soft features that belie the chrome underneath — people underestimate them once, usually only once. The chrome is visible — wired reflexes with adrenaline pump — chemical-mechanical hybrid augmentation — and they make no effort to hide it.

They came up through the Shelf's informal apprentice system, learning the trade from runners who didn't survive long enough to see them surpass them. They work as a saboteur out of The Circuit, taking contracts that match their skills and their risk tolerance, which are higher than most people consider healthy.

In a city full of people who talk about what they'll do, Chiamaka Aguilar-Annan are one of the ones who actually does it.

core_fears: Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks
Being captured alive — death is preferable to corporate interrogation
Losing their edge to age — the body slows before the mind accepts it
core_desires: To find the person who burned them and make it educational
Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again
Justice — the corporate kind, where the punishment fits the profit margin
coping_mechanisms: Overwork — takes every contract offered because idleness invites thinking
Drinks methodically — not to get drunk, to maintain a specific level of not-caring
Connection — finds someone to talk to, even if it's a bartender or a cat
blind_spots: Believes their trauma makes them special instead of recognizing it as damage to manage
Cannot distinguish between caution and cowardice in themselves or others
Assumes everyone has an angle because they always have an angle
psychology.secret: Chiamaka Aguilar-Annan sends anonymous tips to Meridian 88 law enforcement about competitors. It's not principle — it's market manipulation.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Educated vocabulary wrapped in street delivery — the contrast is deliberate.
speech_patterns.cadence: Low and even — the vocal equivalent of still water.
verbal_tics: Addresses people by physical traits — 'hey, tall one' or 'listen, chrome-arm'
Uses technical jargon for everything, including emotions
example_lines: "I don't break things. I introduce structural critiques."
"The most effective sabotage looks like bad luck."
"Everything has a weakness. Infrastructure has thousands."

story_hooks: A former associate resurfaces with evidence that could destroy Chiamaka Aguilar-Annan's reputation — and a price for silence
A Tier 4 executive offers Chiamaka Aguilar-Annan a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten
Chiamaka Aguilar-Annan is offered a contract that would clear all their debts — the target is someone they respect
narrative_function: Chiamaka Aguilar-Annan functions as a connector — their work puts them in contact with multiple factions, classes, and agendas. Stories involving them naturally cross boundaries between districts, tiers, and moral categories.
augmentations: Wired reflexes with adrenaline pump — chemical-mechanical hybrid augmentation. Reflex boosters wired into spinal column — shaves reaction time by 40ms
daily_life: Between contracts, maintains a cover identity — mundane work, mundane hours, mundane neighbors. The transition from civilian to runner and back requires a conscious effort that gets easier with practice and more disturbing with self-awareness.
affiliation: Independent — known in Old Harbor circles

decision_rules: Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
Will not betray a client who paid in full, regardless of better offers
Maintains a personal blacklist of clients who've burned runners — checks it religiously
Will not take contracts against children or families — the line is hard and non-negotiable
escalation_ladder: 1. Assess — read the situation, identify threats and advantages
2. Negotiate — try to find a solution that doesn't cost ammunition
3. Intimidate — make the cost of conflict clear
4. Precision violence — surgical, targeted, minimal collateral
5. Full engagement — overwhelming force, no half measures
6. Emergency protocol — abort mission, survival priority, deal with consequences later

interpersonal_modes.employers: Guarded respect. They pay, the job gets done. Anything beyond that is liability.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Loyal but reserved. Trusts their competence, withholds personal information by reflex.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Superficially friendly, internally cataloguing exits and weapons. The smile is real; the relaxation isn't.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Predatory focus. Threats are problems, and problems have solutions. The solution is usually kinetic.

stress_responses.low: Channels it into preparation — checks gear, reviews plans, contacts sources.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Hyper-focused tunnel vision. Peripheral concerns disappear. Only the threat exists.
stress_responses.critical: Berserker clarity. Everything becomes simple: survive. Deal with the rest later. The simplicity is almost peaceful.

contradictions: Despises corporate culture but has unconsciously adopted its efficiency metrics and self-optimization language
Presents as emotionless professional but is deeply affected by collateral damage
Projects confidence but makes decisions from a foundation of fear they've never examined
habits: Saves a percentage of every payment in physical Quanta, hidden in the walls of their space
Counts ammunition obsessively — knows the exact round count at all times
Never drinks anything they didn't see poured or open themselves
breaking_points: Learning that a job they completed resulted in mass casualties they weren't told about
Discovering their employer deliberately sent them into a death trap
Losing their primary augmentation — the one that defines their professional identity
